How does Hitha eliminate cryptographic hash chain concurrency forks during high throughput Virtual Thread bursts? Root Cause : In AuditLogServiceImpl , concurrent Java 21 Virtual Threads reading the latest parent hash simultaneously via findLatestHashChainValue under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED isolation read the exact same uncommitted parent, resulting in parallel hash branches and breaking verification. Architectural Solution : We serialized hash calculation and insertion using an explicit JVM ReentrantLock hashChainLock wrapping the parent lookup, computeHashV2 , and repository save. Verification : Verified with AuditLogServiceConcurrencyTest executing 20 simultaneous Virtual Threads writing audit logs concurrently. title: Enterprise Dual-Plane Logging & Storage Architecture
preview:
id: dual plane architecture title: Enterprise Dual Plane Logging & Storage Architecture sidebar label: Dual Plane Architecture slug: /logging audit/dual plane architecture Enterprise Dual Plane Logging & Storage Architecture Telehealth systems generate massive amounts of telemetry: debug traces, query execution timings, client heartbeats, clinical document accesses, and payment events. Traditional single destination logging creates two catastrophic failure modes: 1. The Disk Full Crash : Writing all logs to local disk without strict rolling limits fills the server drive and crashes containers. 2. The Database Bloat Crash : Writing every trace, click, or authentication denial into PostgreSQL inflates table sizes to gigabytes, exhausts the 8 connection HikariCP pool, and halts clinical bookings. To permanently solve this, HITHA enforces the Dual Plane Logging Strategy .

title: PostgreSQL Indexing Optimization & Block Range (BRIN) Performance
preview: id: database indexing optimization title: PostgreSQL Indexing Optimization & Block Range BRIN Performance sidebar label: PostgreSQL Indexing & BRIN slug: /reference/database indexing optimization PostgreSQL Indexing Optimization & Block Range BRIN Performance Poor indexing strategies degrade transactional throughput. HITHA continuously tunes its indexing architecture across high volume tables. 🚀 Key Indexing Remediations BRIN Architecture : Block Range Indexes record only the minimum and maximum column values for ranges of physical pages on disk. For naturally ordered time series data like audit logs.created at , BRIN yields near B Tree search speeds with less than 1% of the disk and buffer cache footprint. Composite B Tree Indexes : Query plans involving multiple WHERE clauses e.g. WHERE doctor id = ? AND date = ? use composite keys to avoid expensive bitmap index heap scans.

title: Server-Sent Events (SSE) & Seamless Token Refresh Lifecycle
preview: id: sse token refresh title: Server Sent Events SSE & Seamless Token Refresh Lifecycle sidebar label: SSE & JWT Renewal Handshake slug: /security/sse token refresh Server Sent Events SSE & Seamless Token Refresh Lifecycle Real time notifications in HITHA appointment bookings, payment confirmations, doctor call rings are delivered using persistent Server Sent Events SSE over HTTP streaming. 🔄 The Token Expiration Handshake Mechanism : The backend runs an SSE heartbeat loop. When an active connection's JWT token approaches expiration, the server emits a structured TOKEN EXPIRED WARNING event over the established stream. Client Handshake : The frontend intercepts this event, triggers a background refresh request to /api/v1/auth/refresh token , receives a fresh token, and acknowledges the active connection without re establishing TCP handshakes. Failure Resilience : If token renewal fails, the connection terminates gracefully with an explicit redirect to the re authentication page rather than hanging in a dead socket state.
